independentCheck.sourceAnswerStatus: publisher Q/3 matches reversible Carnot ratio exactly provided T is absolute and positive

items.reviewClassification: original calculation scientifically consistent; compulsory reversible-ratio/cognitive-level explanation
items.reviewReason: The original question explicitly identifies a Carnot engine, names heat absorbed Q at temperature T, and gives a cold reservoir T/3. The reversible Carnot relationship therefore implies Q_C/Q_H=(T/3)/T=1/3, reproducing the publisher's Q/3. Q_C denotes the POSITIVE MAGNITUDE of rejected heat; the signed heat transferred to the working substance on the cold isotherm is −Q/3. A general irreversible heat engine does not obey this exact heat ratio. The printed SLO P-11-C-23 is Knowledge but computing a symbolic heat ratio is an Application task, so teacher mapping remains pending.

items.sloFit: closest printed theory SLO concerns entropy as degree of disorder (Understanding); it does not directly authenticate quantitative phase-change entropy calculation for summative use

independentCheck.usualIceLatentHeatCaveat: The problem-implied latent heat 250 kJ/kg differs from usual tabulated ~334 kJ/kg; keep the supplied 500 J for 2 g as authoritative for this exercise.
independentCheck.scopeOfEntropy: Negative entropy change belongs to the freezing 70 g of water, not to the refrigerator plus surroundings; refrigeration requires external work and the total isolated entropy balance cannot be inferred from this one ΔS.

items.reviewClassification: source answer and sign consistent using its own latent energy; compulsory material-specific input and subsystem/SLO qualifications
items.reviewReason: Original p.153 supplies 500 J to melt 2 g at 0°C, then asks for the entropy change of 70 g of water at 0°C when it freezes in a refrigerator. This fixes a source-specific latent energy of 250 J/g, which should not be replaced with a standard tabulated fusion value. Freezing reverses melting, so heat Q for the water is negative, −500(70/2)=−17,500 J, and ΔS of the WATER is −17,500/273.15≈−64.07 J/K. The printed −64 J K⁻¹ is consistent after rounding. This does not establish the total refrigerator+room entropy balance; no direct summative entropy-numerical SLO has been authenticated in original V224 Domain C.

items.reviewClassification: source arithmetic correct; compulsory retain both calculation and pressure–volume diagram for completed question
items.reviewReason: Printed original Numerical 8.9 has TWO explicit subparts: (a) calculate work done BY gas from 1 m³ to 2 m³ at constant atmospheric pressure, and (b) represent the work on a PV diagram. Using 1 atm≈1.013×10⁵ Pa, ΔV=+1 m³, W_by=PΔV=+1.013×10⁵ J matches the printed value. At the more exact 101325 Pa the answer is 101325 J, rounding consistently. A complete marking scheme needs a labeled P–V plot with a rightward horizontal isobar and area below it between the two volumes; a numerical answer alone fails the printed part (b). The pressure/volume model treats the gas expansion as quasistatic against the stated constant ambient pressure.
items.independentVariantRequirement: A separate independently drawn accessible P–V schematic can be proposed for teacher review before students see the answer; preserve original printed a/b question and do not invent a publisher diagram.
